title: Quantization Deployment Safeguard Framework for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Ship a repeatable, safety-first deployment framework for enabling FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) profiles on Hopper GPUs with automated calibration, staged rollouts, and deterministic rollback guarantees. Scope covers: an automated calibration runner (golden seeds + dataset sampling), per-layer scaling verification, latency and jitter telemetry baselines, canary gating heuristics, and a fail-safe that reverts requests to stable INT8 variants when accuracy or tail latency thresholds are breached. This ticket focuses on the orchestration and guardrails so model teams can opt into FP8 with low operational risk.

Key pieces: 
- Calibration harness: orchestrates offline and online calibration passes, records per-op scales, and stores canonical quant metadata. Supports seeding, repeatable RNG, and a "shadow" inference mode that computes FP8 outputs in parallel for statistical validation.
- Golden evaluation: curated prompt set (500 examples across short/long tail, safety-sensitive cases) with automated accuracy metrics (perplexity delta, top-k token differences, structured-output schema checks).
- Canary orchestration: progressive traffic ramp (0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50%) with automatic hold/rollback on metric violations. Metrics: average token-level divergence, accuracy regression (>0.5% flag), 99.9th latency delta (>15% flag), error-rate spike (>2x baseline).
- Telemetry & alerts: new telemetry keys (quant.deploy.latency_tail, quant.deploy.token_divergence, quant.deploy.shadow_mismatch_rate). Dashboards and SLOs added to Console.
- Rollback primitives: instant routing rule flip to INT8 model variant, with stateful KPIs persisted for postmortem. Hysteresis and cool-down windows to prevent flapping.

Out-of-scope: core kernel optimizations and per-chip micro-tuning (handled by runtime/infra tickets). This ticket coordinates integration points and the safety automation so that enabling FP8 becomes a low-friction product feature for both Hosted and Dedicated customers.

2025-02-22: PM feedback from Priya Kapoor: require explicit "opt-in" switch per project and a visible badge in Console indicating FP8 is active. Added to scope as UI acceptance criteria.

2025-02-28: Validation run against golden set (N=500) on hopper-e5m2: 99.7% of examples within 0.5% accuracy threshold. Two structured-output regressions identified (invoice-date extraction). Created follow-up ENG subtask to add targeted calibration for date tokens (ENG-831556).

2025-03-01: Review with runtime team (lead: Sanjay Rao). Decision: use hysteresis window of 10 minutes for rollback to avoid flapping; require 3 consecutive evaluation windows to trigger automatic rollback. Runtime will expose a circuit-breaker API by 2025-03-10.

2025-03-03: Canary plan approved by SRE. Canary percentages and hold conditions codified in canary-config.yaml in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-deploy/PR-6492. QA to run chaos experiment that kills 1/3 of quant nodes during 10% ramp to validate graceful fallback.
2025-03-04: Blocker: need dataset approval from privacy/compliance for one customer-specific golden set. Engaging Privacy team; until approval, that customer will be excluded from auto-canary.
